extracted.intended_audience: aspiring writers, poets, and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writers (especially poets and moral/essay writers) on when similarity becomes plagiarism, how to achieve perceived originality (through form, mode, and contemporary detail), and what qualities make pastoral and sentimental poetry effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity is not plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: A coincidence of sentiment may easily happen without any communication, since there are many occasions in which all reasonable men will nearly think alike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accuse an author of plagiarism simply because his sentiments or images resemble those of earlier writers; shared objects of speculation, passions, and social relations naturally produce likenesses of thought and expression. Examples: historians relating the same facts or moralists teaching the same immutable rights will necessarily agree in many particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the subject before charging plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary... that before an author be charged with plagiarism... the subject on which he treats should be carefully considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different subjects (history, science, morality, passions) constrain writers toward similar formulations. Only when resemblance cannot be explained by common subject-matter or natural response should accusations of plagiarism be entertained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality through choice of mode and form
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many modes of composition, by which a moralist may deserve the name of an original writer: he may familiarize his system by dialogues... subtilize it into a series of syllogistick arguments... enforce his doctrine by seriousness and solemnity, or enliven it by sprightliness and gaiety... deliver his sentiments in naked precepts, or illustrate them by historical examples... continue discourse, or short strictures, and unconnected essays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality can be achieved by selecting or innovating in form and mode. Excellence in any chosen form—dialogue, formal argument, lively essays, sober precepts, extended discourse—can attract distinct readerships; writers should cultivate the form that best fits their genius and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use novelty and fashion to reach contemporaries
rubrics_metrics.description: A new book often seizes the attention of the publick, without any other claim than that it is new... there is likewise in composition, as in other things, a perpetual vicissitude of fashion; and truth is recommended at one time by appearances which at another would expose it to neglect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To engage current readers, writers should be aware of contemporary tastes and fashions; novelty in presentation or topical framing can make otherwise familiar truths feel fresh and persuasive to a particular generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe changing social particulars to refresh universal passions
rubrics_metrics.description: They are to observe the alterations which time is always making in the modes of life, that they may gratify every generation with a picture of themselves... Thus love is uniform, but courtship is perpetually varying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since core passions are constant but the external forms (manners of courtship, ambitions, occupations, vices) change, authors should root universal emotional states in up-to-date social particulars to create immediacy and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce variety by combining and modifying a few passions
rubrics_metrics.description: The passions of the mind... are very few; but those few agitated and combined, as external causes shall happen to operate, and modified by prevailing opinions and accidental caprices, make such frequent alterations on the surface of life, that the show... vanishes from the view, and a new set of objects succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should mix and vary fundamental passions with differing external circumstances, opinions, and accidental details to generate endless imaginative variety—analogous to mixing a few primary colours to produce many tints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth derived from real events often outperforms artful fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: These two poems were produced by events that really happened; and may, therefore, be of use to prove, that we can always feel more than we can imagine, and that the most artful fiction must give way to truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchoring poetry or narrative in real occurrences can produce more powerful feeling and credibility than contrived invention; authenticity of experience often yields stronger emotional resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pastoral poetry: naturalness and diversity of feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: The first and the tenth pastorals... are sufficient to place their author above the reach of rivalry... The first... is equally natural and more diversified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective pastoral poetry should exhibit naturalness (believable voice and sentiment) and variety (diverse imagery and circumstances). A pastoral's excellence lies in sincere emotional expression and a range of rural detail rather than artificial uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic expression of disappointed love
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint of Gallus disappointed in his love, is full of such sentiments as disappointed love naturally produces; his wishes are wild, his resentment is tender, and his purposes are inconstant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depictions of romantic despair should mirror the real, often-contradictory states of mind (wild wishes, tender resentment, inconstancy). Realistic, internally consistent emotional nuances make love complaints convincing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid rural imagery to evoke solace or contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: He catches the idea of rural tranquillity... 'Here cooling fountains roll through flow'ry meads, Here woods... lift their verdant heads'... But notwithstanding the excellence of the tenth pastoral, I cannot forbear to give the preference to the first, which is equally natural and more diversified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pastoral or descriptive scenes should employ concrete sensory images (fountains, meads, woods, willows, bees, songs) to evoke either solace or a poignant contrast with the speaker's condition. Variety and specificity strengthen emotional impact.
